text: . The government has said that more than one crore 73  lakh e-Passports have been issued so far in India and abroad. In a written reply in Rajya Sabha today, Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh said that currently, all Regional Passport Offices, Passport Seva Kendras and Post Office Passport Seva Kendras in India and all the Indian Missions abroad are issuing e-Passports. He informed that the e-Passport was launched in May last year. Mr Singh said that the Passport Seva Programme provided comprehensive digital platforms. This includes the Passport Seva Portal, Passport Seva Mobile Apps and a centralised citizen service call centre, enabling applicants to access information, track application status and obtain responses to routine queries without visiting Regional Passport Offices. The Minister said, these digital initiatives have substantially reduced the need for physical visits for administrative enquiries while improving accessibility, convenience and service delivery.

. Arunachal’s para shuttler Biri Takar has clinched Double Medal at BWF Para World Circuit in Brazil. Takar has won Gold in Men’s Doubles and Bronze in Men’s Singles. Arunachal Pradesh Chief Minister Pema Khandu congratulated the sportsman for his international achievements.Congratulating the athlete, Chief Minister in a social media post highlighted that Takar is a beneficiary of the Chief Minister’s Award to Champion Excellence in Sports (CM ACES) programme.  and said his international success reflects the programme growing impact on nurturing sporting talent in the state.

. India has urged Sri Lanka to cooperate in the early release of Indian fishermen and their boats detained by its authorities, while reiterating that a humanitarian approach should guide the handling of the long-pending issue. The matter figured prominently during Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri’s discussions with the Sri Lankan leadership during his official visit to Colombo.Mr Misri arrived in Colombo yesterday for a day-long visit. He held separate meetings with President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya, Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath and Foreign Secretary Aruni Ranaraja. During the talks, Mr Misri discussed issues pertaining to fishermen and requested Sri Lanka’s cooperation for the early release of fishermen and boats detained in the island nation. The fishermen issue is a contentious one in the ties between India and Sri Lanka, with Lankan Navy personnel even firing at Indian fishermen in the Palk Strait and seizing their boats in several alleged incidents of illegally entering Sri Lankan territorial waters.

. Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has projected GDP growth to 6.7 percent in this fiscal year, deciding to keep the Repo rate unchanged at 5.25 percent with neutral stance. RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra has said that country’s economic growth continues to be supported by resilient demand and it remains world’s fastest growing large economy. He said, country’s economy has performed better than expected in April-June quarter of this fiscal year.Announcing the Monetary Policy Committee’s decision today, Mr. Malhotra said, RBI has decided to keep repo rate unchanged at 5.25 percent and retained a neutral stance. Repo rate is the interest rate at which the central bank lends short-term money to commercial banks against government securities.He said, RBI has lowered CPI inflation projection to 5 percent from earlier estimate of 5.1 percent for financial year 2027. The Governor said the recent rise in inflation was largely driven by food and fuel prices rather than broad-based demand pressures.Mr. Malhotra said, economy had performed better than expected during the first quarter of the financial year, prompting the central bank to revise its real GDP growth projection for 2026-27 to 6.7 per cent. The RBI Governor said, West Asia conflict continues to challenge global economy by disrupting key trade routes.RBI struck an optimistic note on the domestic economy, raising its growth projection for 2026-27 while lowering its inflation forecast, saying robust exports, steady investment activity and easing supply-side disruptions have strengthened the macroeconomic outlook despite persistent global uncertainties.On the external front, the RBI said foreign direct investment inflows remained robust while foreign portfolio investment has witnessed a turnaround in recent months. The Governor said, country’s foreign exchange reserves remain comfortable at nearly 693 billion US dollars, providing import cover of more than ten months.RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra has said that Polymer notes are expected to be in circulation at the beginning of next financial year, if everything goes as per schedule. Addressing a press conference in Mumbai, Mr. Malhotra said, Polymer notes enhances durability. He said that details about the security features and other will be communicated soon. While talking about Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) and Unified Lending Interface, Deputy Governor Rohit Jain said that its uses is increasing and various stakeholders are accepting it.

. India and Singapore have reviewed the progress of bilateral cooperation under the eight areas outlined by the Roadmap for India-Singapore Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. The 19th round of India-Singapore Foreign Office Consultations was held in New Delhi yesterday.The meeting was co-chaired by Secretary (East), Rudrendra Tandon, and Permanent Secretary (Policy), Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Singapore, Luke Goh. Both sides also exchanged views on regional and global developments and reaffirmed the importance of close coordination at international and regional fora, including ASEAN, in addressing shared challenges.The External Affairs Ministry said in a statement that India-Singapore relations were elevated to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership during the visit of Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Singapore in September 2024. The Roadmap for Comprehensive Strategic Partnership was launched during the visit of Prime Minister of Singapore, Lawrence Wong, to India in September last year. It covers cooperation in several areas, including Economic Cooperation, Skills Development, Digitalisation, Sustainability, Connectivity, and Healthcare and Medicine.

. India has successfully test-fired the medium-range ballistic missile Agni-4 from the Integrated Test Range at Chandipur in Odisha. The Defence Ministry said the launch validated all operational and technical parameters of the missile. The test was carried out under the aegis of the Strategic Forces Command. The Ministry added that the successful launch marks another milestone in strengthening the country’s strategic deterrence capabilities.Defence Minister Rajnath Singh congratulated the Strategic Forces Command and DRDO on the successful mission. In a social media post, the Defence Minister reaffirmed India’s commitment to defend the Nation with state-of-the-art technologies.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has urged every citizen to celebrate National Handloom Day today with enthusiasm and joy. Sharing a video message, Mr Modi said that on August 7, 1905, the Swadeshi Movement was launched as part of India’s struggle for independence and people from all walks of life united and fought a historic battle against British rule.He encouraged people to support poor weaving families and artisans who create fabrics with their own hands. Further, Prime Minister highlighted the importance of strengthening these small and economically disadvantaged weaving families to build a self-reliant country.Mr Modi also appealed to the countrymen to purchase at least one handloom product, make a video about it, and share it across the country and the world so that the skill and craftsmanship of India’s artisans receive global recognition.National Handloom Day is observed every year on the 7th of August to commemorate the Swadeshi Movement launched on the same day in 1905.On the occasion of National Handloom Day, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that on this day the country celebrates its rich and vibrant handloom heritage. Conveying salutations to the skill, creativity and dedication of the weavers and artisans of the country, Mr Modi said that for generations, they have preserved and enriched the traditions of India.Sharing a social media post, Mr Modi noted that the Government will keep supporting the handloom sector, which is an important pillar of rural empowerment, women-led development and fulfilling the dream of an Atmanirbhar Bharat. He urged the citizens to share their favourite handloom products and make videos using the hashtag NationalHandloomDay. He added that this will encourage the craftsmen who are associated with the sector.

. The Government today said that it has strengthened the legal and institutional framework to deal with online piracy of cinematograph films, including unauthorized dissemination of films through intermediaries such as Telegram. In a written reply in Lok Sabha today, Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting Dr. L Murugan said, the Cinematograph Act, 1952 was amended through the Cinematograph (Amendment) Act, 2023 to introduce specific provisions to curb unauthorized recording and exhibition of films. The Minister also said that the newly inserted Section 7(1B)(ii) empowers the Government, under Section 79(3) of the Information Technology Act, 2000, to take action against intermediaries hosting pirated content. Mr. Murugan informed that under the Information Technology Rules, 2021, the intermediaries are required to remove any content violative of any law for the time being in force as and when brought to their knowledge either through a court order or through a notice by appropriate government or its authorized agency.

. The Lok Sabha has passed a Bill to amend the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, authorising the government to permit banks and other service providers to levy charges on payments made through the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) and other notified electronic payment modes. The government’s approach aims to levy small charge on digital payment services for consumers and small businesses while ensuring a sustainable revenue model for banks, payment service providers (PSPs), and payment infrastructure firms that drive the digital payments ecosystem.The amendment passed by the House seeks to remove the existing legal provision that prevents banks and payment service providers from charging Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on notified electronic payment modes. While real-time payments made through RTGS and NEFT already attract service charges, UPI transactions have so far remained exempt from such fees. The proposed changes in the Payment and Settlement Systems Act are a part of comprehensive legislation on taxation, which was introduced in the House on Tuesday.The Bill was passed through a voice vote in the Lok Sabha after the House resumed at 2 pm after the earlier adjournment. As soon as the House reassembled, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman moved the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, further to amend the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 and the Income Tax Act, 2025, and to amend the Finance Act, 2026, to be taken into consideration.

. The countdown to the 2030 Ahmedabad Commonwealth Games has officially begun, with the curtain falling on the Glasgow Commonwealth Games last night. As the curtain came down, India offered the world a vibrant invitation to Ahmedabad, blending ancient philosophy, contemporary artistry and cultural grandeur in a handover presentation that officially launched the journey towards the centenary edition of the Games in 2030.Prince Edward, Duke of Edinburgh, representing King Charles III, formally declared the Games closed in Glasgow. He called up on athletes of all countries and territories to visit Ahmedabad in four years’ time to celebrate the 24th Commonwealth Games.The formal handover began with the Commonwealth Games flag making its symbolic journey across the arena. Led by bearers holding the Scottish and Indian flags, the procession lowered the folded Games flag. Glasgow’s Lord Provost Jacqueline McLaren then passed it to Commonwealth Games Scotland vice-chair Susan Jackson, two-time Olympic medallist Neeraj Chopra, Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha, and finally Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi.This marked the official transfer of hosting responsibilities from Scotland to India. India last hosted the Commonwealth Games in New Delhi in 2010. After 11 days of intense competition, Indian athletes departed from Glasgow as a satisfied bunch after winning 39 medals at the 2026 Games, including 13 gold, 17 silver, and nine bronze, to end in fourth position on the standings.

. Hockey India today announced the 18-member Indian junior women’s team for the AHF Junior Asia Cup 2026, to be held in Moqi, China, from August 30 to September 13.The squad comprises 18 players along with two alternate players and will be led by midfielder Khaidem Shileima Chanu. The team heads into the tournament after an extensive training camp under newly appointed head coach Tim White, who took charge earlier this year.The tournament will bring together the continent’s leading junior teams, serving as a key platform for the next generation of Asian hockey talent. The match schedule and pool compositions will be announced closer to the start of the tournament.
. In the forex market today, the rupee depreciated by 10 paise to end at 95 rupees and 22 paise against the US dollar.

. Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya today felicitated Indian athletes who returned from the Commonwealth Games 2026 after delivering historic performances in boxing, judo and para-athletics. During the felicitation ceremony held in New Delhi, the medal winners were presented cash awards of 30 lakh rupees for gold, 20 lakh rupees for silver and 10 lakh rupees for bronze.Interacting with the athletes, Dr. Mandaviya asked the athletes to think beyond their playing careers and become contributors to the next generation of Indian sport. The Minister highlighted the revamped Khelo India scheme of worth rupees 36,000 crore. He said that this initiative will take care of greater continued investment in the growth of Indian sports in the coming years. Congratulating the champions, Dr. Mandaviya urged them to extend their contribution to Indian sport beyond their competitive careers by mentoring and inspiring the next generation of athletes.

. Young cyclist Harshita Jakhar rode into history books by becoming the first Indian woman to be a part of the Tour de France Femmes in Switzerland. The 19-year-old led a pack of eight talented cyclists from Afghanistan, Algeria, Chile, Ethiopia with two riders, Namibia and Uganda during the ceremonial start at Stage 2 of the gruelling race yesterday. The event started on 1st of this month in Lausanne and will end on 9th August in Nice.The team, handpicked by UCI (Union Cycliste de Internationale), cycled 4.5 kilometres on a neutralised section of the course along with some riders from the WCC Road Team.Tour de France Femmes is the women’s multi-stage cycling race that corresponds to the men’s Tour de France. It is part of the UCI Women’s World Tour calendar.UCI President David Lappartient joined the riders on the start podium before the stage and expressed his delight at seeing an Indian in the mix.Hailing from Rajasthan, Harshita has been making waves on the Indian cycling circuit, sweeping almost all the medals on offer in junior category and winning regularly in the seniors section as well. Her aim is to finish among the Top 10 at the 2026 Asian Games, and win a medal in the 2030 Games.

. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has stated that the ambition of the Government is to create a society where modern progress is anchored in civilisational heritage. Addressing the CD Deshmukh Lecture 2026 in New Delhi, Ms Sitharaman said India’s destiny is to become prosperous without becoming consumerist, wealthy without becoming materialistic and globally successful without losing its civilisational character.She added that India’s aim is to become a developed civilisation that combines prosperity with trusteeship, enterprise with responsibility, innovation with civilisational wisdom, global leadership with cultural rootedness, environmental stewardship with economic progress, and individual success with collective welfare.

. The Supreme Court today directed the central government to develop a pilot project linking fuel sales to valid third-party motor insurance, proposing that uninsured vehicles be denied fuel at petrol pumps until coverage is obtained. A bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Prashant Kumar Mishra said nearly 56 percent of vehicles on Indian roads are uninsured and called the situation shocking.The court directed the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India and the Centre to pilot Automatic Number Plate Recognition,ANPR-based insurance verification to identify uninsured vehicles and improve compliance with the Motor Vehicles Act.The bench also directed the Centre to launch pilot projects on selected national highway corridors to replace conventional toll plazas with automatic vehicle detection systems, aiming to reduce congestion and improve traffic flow.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended in positive zone for the second straight session today . The Sensex gained 374 points or nearly half a per cent to close at 78,955. The Nifty rose marginally by 11 points to settle at 24,636.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index dipped over 0.4 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index added nearly half a per cent.After opening higher, the Sensex maintained positive momentum throughout the session. Meanwhile the Nifty traded in a narrow-range, recovering from the slight dips witnessed during the intra-day trade.In the Sensex pack, 16 out of 30 companies registered losses. Among the top laggards, Power Grid lost four per cent, Tata Consultancy Services shed over two per cent and Indigo dropped nearly one and a half per cent. In contrast, Reliance climbed over 3.4 per cent, State Bank of India increased three per cent and Bharat Electronics Limited rose 2.5 per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 15 out of 28 sectors ended in the positive zone. Among the top gainers, PSU Bank advanced over two per cent, Capital Goods rose nearly 1.3 per cent and Energy gained over 1.1 per cent. In contrast, Realty dipped over 1.4 per cent, Services shed 1.1 per cent and Utilities lost over one per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2,161 companies declined, 2,117 advanced and 215 remained unchanged.

. The Ministry of Textiles will organise a national function at the Rashtrapati Bhavan Cultural Centre today to celebrate 12th National Handloom Day. President Droupadi Mumru will join the event as the chief guest, with Union Textiles Minister Giriraj Singh and Minister of State Pabitra Margherita attending the programme.The Textiles Ministry said that the function aims to celebrate India’s rich handloom heritage and recognise the contribution of the handloom weaving community to the nation’s cultural and economic development. Akashvani correspondent reports that a major highlight of the celebrations will be the presentation of the Sant Kabir Handloom Awards and the National Handloom Awards for the year 2025.A total of 22 awards, comprising three Sant Kabir Handloom Awards and nineteen National Handloom Awards, will be conferred upon the handloom weavers for their craftsmanship, innovation and contribution to the preservation of India’s handloom traditions. Four commemorative postage stamps celebrating the country’s rich and diverse handloom weaving traditions will be released on the occasion. Two publications-Earth. Root. Thread – Aal Dyed Handloom Textiles of Central India and the Handloom Awards Book 2025 will also be unveiled during the function.On the sidelines, an exhibition will be organised showcasing award-winning handloom products. Visitors will also have an opportunity to witness live demonstrations of traditional Kani weaving and Wall Hanging weaving, providing a glimpse into the diversity and craftsmanship of India’s handloom traditions.National Handloom Day is observed every year on August 7, to commemorate the Swadeshi Movement launched on the same day in 1905. According to the Ministry of Textiles, the day has served as an occasion to celebrate the artistry, skill and dedication of the Country’s handloom weavers since its inception in the year 2015.

. The country’s coal supply position for the power sector continues to remain adequate, backed by robust growth in production, despatch and receipts during the last month. Ministry of Coal informed that the overall coal production during the previous month stood at over 69 Million Tonnes (MT), as against more than 64 MT during the corresponding period last year. Overall coal despatch during the month stood even higher, at more than 86 MT compared to over 73 MT in the same period last year, marking a robust growth of more than 18 percent.The Ministry said that it remains fully committed to ensuring uninterrupted and adequate coal supply to all consumers, particularly the power sector, to support the nation’s growing energy needs.

. Widening use of security powers by Pakistani forces has increased human rights concerns in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, PoJK. Over the past decade, the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights and several other international organisations have repeatedly raised concerns over enforced disappearances, excessive use of force, restrictions on freedom of expression, and lack of accountability in the occupied territory. On July 27, the first day of so-called legislative elections in PoJK, violent clashes broke out in Rawalakot, with the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) alleging that Pakistani security forces used live ammunition against protesters, resulting in several deaths and injuries.A report in Brussels-based EU Reporter has highlighted that the ongoing shutdown of mobile and internet services made independent verification difficult, restricting the ability of journalists and human rights groups to assess the situation on the ground. According to the report, counterterrorism laws and emergency measures are increasingly being applied to manage routine political dissent in the PoJK.

. Government has operationalized the Inventory-based Cross-border E-Commerce Export Framework under the Foreign Trade Policy 2023. The framework provides a comprehensive policy and procedural architecture for facilitating inventory-based cross-border e-commerce exports of goods manufactured or produced in India. It incorporates several safeguards to ensure that the benefits of e-commerce exports accrue to Indian manufacturers and MSMEs while maintaining regulatory oversight.The Framework also enables export-only inventory operations through registered exporters-on-record. It also provides for timely payments to Indian sellers within the prescribed timeline, irrespective of the receipt of payment from overseas buyers. Ministry of Commerce and Industry said that the framework is expected to facilitate greater participation of Indian manufacturers, traders and MSMEs in global e-commerce supply chains by providing access to organized fulfillment networks while ensuring transparency, timely payments, effective pass-through of export benefits and robust regulatory oversight.
. In the Indian bullion market, 24 carat gold was trading 0.4 percent up at 1,49,340 rupees per 10 grams, while silver was trading 0.6 percent down at 2,27,030 rupees per kilogram, a short while ago.

. In a significant initiative to encourage and promote emerging filmmaking talent from the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir, the Department of Information and Public Relations (DIPR) has announced the IFFJK Emerging Filmmakers Competition 2026, as part of the scheduled 1st International Film Festival of Jammu & Kashmir (IFFJK). Registrations for the competition has commenced from today. Akashvani Jammu Correspondent reports that the competition is exclusively open to aspiring filmmakers from J&K and aims to provide a prestigious platform for young storytellers to showcase their creativity, cinematic vision and technical skills through original short films.The aspiring and emerging filmmakers are invited to submit original short films with a maximum duration of five minutes and the last date for submission is August 26. The applicants must be between 18 and 39 years of age as on September 1, 2026, and possess a valid domicile certificate of J&K. The competition is being organised around the theme “Rang-e-Cinema: Frames of a New Jammu & Kashmir”, reflecting the evolving cultural, social and creative narratives of the region while encouraging youth to present compelling stories through the medium of cinema. Interested filmmakers and cinematographers are advised to register by visiting the official IFFJK website www.iffjk.org and the detailed guidelines, eligibility criteria and the registration process are also available on this website for ease of aspirants. DIPR urges aspiring filmmakers from across J&K to seize this opportunity and contribute towards strengthening the Union Territory’s growing film culture through innovative and impactful storytelling.

. In Badminton, India’s Tanvi Sharma, Ashmita Chaliha and Rakshitha Ramraj have progressed to the Women singles quarterfinals at the Korea Masters in Asan. Tanvi continued her impressive run by defeating her compatriot Shriyanshi Valishetty 21-16, 17-21, 21-13 in the pre-quarterfinals. Ashmita beat home favourite Kim Min-ji 21-17, 21-6, while Rakshitha defeated Japan’s Manami Suizu 22-20, 21-10. However, Anmol Kharb’s, Isharani Baruah’s and Mansi Singh’s Korea Masters campaign came to an end in the pre-quarterfinals.In the men’s doubles pre-quarterfinals, the Indian duo of Prithvi Krishnamurthy Roy and Krishna Prasad Garaga defeated a South Korean pair to secure a place in the quarterfinals. All eyes will now be on tomorrow’s women’s singles and men’s doubles quarterfinal matches.

. The two-day BRICS WAVES Bazaar, a premier international marketplace for the creative economy began in Mumbai today. The event, being held under India’s BRICS Presidency brings together over 500 delegates from BRICS members and partners from 21 countries with an aim to create stronger pathways for collaboration across film, television, animation, VFX, gaming, music, digital media and emerging content formats.Information and Broadcasting Secretary, Mr. Chanchal Kumar said WAVES Bazaar seeks to become a platform for the global creative economy where projects are discovered, partnerships are initiated, co-productions are discussed and new markets are opened. Delivering the keynote address in the opening ceremony, Maharashtra’s Minister of Electronics, IT, AI and Culture, Adv. Ashish Shelar said the BRICS WAVES Bazaar is a high-level, curated confluence designed to shape the future of the global creative economy. The event features high-level conferences, keynote addresses, panel discussions, business networking sessions, and curated Business-to-Business meetings.

. US President Donald Trump has signed two executive orders aimed at restricting birthright citizenship and curbing birth tourism. Speaking at the Oval Office, Trump expressed disappointment over the Supreme Court ruling, calling it an unfortunate decision. He added his administration was cracking down very big” on what he called abuses of the US immigration system.According to the White House, one order identifies categories of children of foreign nationals who would not qualify for birthright citizenship under historical exceptions recognised by the Supreme Court, while the second directs the State and Homeland Security departments to end birth tourism, where foreign nationals travel to the US primarily to secure citizenship for their children.The executive actions come weeks after the US Supreme Court ruled in June that children born in the United States to parents who are unlawfully or temporarily present in the country are entitled to automatic US citizenship under the Citizenship Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.

. The Government has said that 60 merchant vessels carrying cargo were safely moved through the Strait of Hormuz despite the heightened security situation in the West Asia region. Replying to a question in Parliament, the government also disclosed that 3,972 Indian seafarers were repatriated from the Gulf region, while a round-the-clock crisis management system handled tens of thousands of distress calls and emails.The government’s response highlights India’s maritime response during the ongoing West Asia crisis, underscoring how New Delhi managed to keep one of the country’s most critical trade arteries functioning even as tensions threatened shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The strategic waterway connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea, and serves as the world’s most critical maritime chokepoint for energy supplies.

. India’s Ambassador to Japan, Nagma Mallick, today laid flowers at the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park and paid tribute to the victims of the atomic bomb. The Indian envoy’s visit to Hiroshima came as the city marked the 81st anniversary of the US atomic bombing.Ambassador Mallick met Hiroshima Governor Mika Yokota and Hiroshima Mayor Kazumi Matsui at a reception where the diplomatic corps in Japan were invited to attend the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Ceremony.On August 6, 1945, a uranium bomb, carried aboard US bomber Enola Gay, was detonated over Hiroshima in the final stages of the Second World War, killing an estimated 140,000 people. Approximately 50,000 people gathered at Peace Memorial Park to pay tribute to the victims of the atomic bomb. Representatives of 121 nations and the European Union participated in the ceremony held at Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park.

. Minister of Tourism and Culture Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today said that cinema is more than entertainment; it is a bridge to culture, heritage and tourism. He said this during a fireside chat with Netflix Co-CEO Ted Sarandos in New Delhi. Mr Shekhawat highlighted that every Indian story has the potential to inspire someone, somewhere in the world, to experience India. The Minister said that India’s ancient civilisation and cultural diversity are its greatest strengths, and platforms like Netflix can play a key role in taking India’s stories and soft power to global audiences. He noted that the ministry’s partnership with Netflix, including the As Seen on Netflix integration on the Incredible India portal, reflects the shared vision of showcasing India’s rich cultural diversity and strengthening its global soft power through authentic storytelling. Mr Shekhawat also stressed that the Centre is working with all stakeholders to provide tourists with a seamless travel experience across the country.On the sidelines of the fireside chat, talking to Akashvani News, Mr  Shekhawat said that the Ministry’s partnerships with platforms such as Netflix, YouTube, Google, and airline companies including IndiGo and Air India are based on non-commercial and mutually beneficial agreements, without financial payments by the government to these companies.He said that these collaborations will promote India’s tourism globally by showcasing the country’s destinations and cultural diversity. The Minister highlighted that visual storytelling plays a crucial role in influencing travellers’ decisions.

. Union Minister for Development of the North Eastern Region, Jyotiraditya Scindia, today met Commonwealth Games gold medallist Mirabai Chanu in New Delhi and congratulated her on winning a record-extending third consecutive Commonwealth Games gold medal in Glasgow. During the meeting, Mr Scindia lauded Mirabai Chanu’s determination and perseverance, and noted that her achievement will inspire young athletes across the country, particularly in the Northeast. They also discussed various aspects of high-performance sports, including training, nutrition, recovery and athlete support.The Minister highlighted the Centre’s efforts to strengthen the sporting ecosystem in the Northeast through the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region’s High-Level Task Force and the One State, One Sport initiative. He said that the primary focus of the Government is to create world-class coaching, scientific training and sports infrastructure, nurturing more champions from the region.

. Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has achieved a 23.66 billion transaction count last month. In a social media post, the Department of Financial Services, under the Ministry of Finance, today thanked citizens for embracing digital payments and driving this revolution forward. It also called people to continue the journey of transforming the way the country transacts.

. Union Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan has dedicated India’s first indigenous MA-104 Cell Line-Based Live Attenuated African Swine Fever (ASF) Vaccine for pigs. The Ministry said that the vaccine is a major breakthrough in veterinary research and is well suited for large-scale production. It said that the vaccine has successfully undergone comprehensive laboratory evaluation, including sterility, purity, safety, genetic stability, immunogenicity, protective efficacy and virulence reversion studies. The vaccine was field validated in collaboration with the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying further establishing its safety and efficacy under field conditions. The vaccine is recommended for healthy pigs above eight weeks of age and is administered as a 1 mL intramuscular injection, followed by a booster dose 14 days after the primary vaccination. Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Rajiv Ranjan Singh was present on the occasion.Speaking on the development, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education, Dr. M.L. Jat said that this breakthrough marks the dawn of a new era in veterinary science. He said that the breakthrough reflects India’s growing scientific capability to develop world-class animal health solutions and paves the way for a new generation of indigenously developed vaccines.Over 1.5 lakh passenger journeys were recorded in a single day on the Delhi-Meerut Namo Bharat on the 3rd of this month.

. The Ministry of Education today opened the online registration portal for Yuva Sangam Phase VII under the Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat initiative. The Ministry said that interested youth aged between 18 and 30 years, including students of Higher Education Institutions, NSS/NYKS volunteers, and young professionals, are eligible to register. It said that for Phase VII, 20 Higher Education Institutions including IITs, IIMs, Central Universities and NITs have been identified as nodal institutions to host and facilitate the exchange programme. Selected participants will undertake five to seven day educational and cultural tours to their paired States and Union Territories. They will gain first-hand exposure to local traditions, educational institutions, governance initiatives, innovation ecosystems, industries, heritage sites, and community life during the exchange programme.

. In United Kingdom, Members of the British Kashmiri diaspora staged a demonstration in Bradford yesterday, expressing solidarity with the people of Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK) and voicing support for the demands of the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC).Protesters gathered in the city centre carrying banners and placards, calling for the protection of fundamental rights, civil liberties and human dignity. Organisers said, the rally was aimed at drawing international attention to what they described as the deteriorating human rights situation in PoJK. Speakers at the demonstration alleged that security operations carried out over the past two months had resulted in civilian casualties, widespread fear and restrictions affecting local communities. They also claimed that women, children and elderly residents had been among those adversely affected. Participants called for transparent and impartial investigations into allegations of excessive use of force, house raids and other reported human rights violations. They urged the authorities to ensure accountability and uphold the rule of law.The demonstrators also appealed to the international community, human rights organisations and the British government to closely monitor developments in PoJK and support efforts to protect fundamental freedoms and promote a peaceful resolution to the issues raised by local communities.

. NASA, the US space agency, has announced that the second stage of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket crashed into the Moon’s surface early today. The impact occurred at 12:05 PM IST.The Falcon 9 rocket was launched on January 15, 2025, carrying two commercial robotic lunar landers. After completing its mission, the rocket’s first stage successfully returned to Earth, while the second stage was left in space to drift.According to scientists, the impact created a crater measuring approximately 20 to 30 metres in diameter on the lunar surface.Researchers said the rare event, an artificial object striking the Moon, provided valuable scientific data, offering new insights into the Moon’s surface and helping improve planning for future lunar exploration missions.

. The Centre has notified the implementation of the Readjustment of Representation of Scheduled Tribes in Assembly Constituencies of the State of Goa Act, 2025, paving the way for the reservation of Assembly seats for Scheduled Tribes in Goa.Akashvani correspondent reports that according to the notification published in The Gazette of India, the Act came into force from 6th August 2026, fulfilling a long-pending demand of the state’s tribal communities and enabling the process of constituency readjustment and reservation.Welcoming the development, Goa Chief Minister Dr. Pramod Sawant described it as a promise fulfilled. In a social media post, he said the Act marks a decisive step towards ensuring long-overdue justice and political representation for the Scheduled Tribe communities. Dr. Sawant thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah for making the legislation a reality, saying it reflects the spirit of “Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas.

. Home Minister Amit Shah has offered salutations to Poet Laureate Gurudev Rabindranath Tagore on his death anniversary. In a social media post, Mr Shah said that Tagore gave voice to the soul of India and infused new consciousness into the freedom movement through his writings.The Minister added that Tagore’s immortal creation ‘Jana Gana Mana’ is a symbol of the nation’s unified consciousness and self-pride. Further, Mr Shah noted that the Poet Laureate elevated the glory of Indian culture, philosophy, and education onto the global stage by establishing Visva-Bharati University. The Home Minister underlined that Tagore’s literature remains an inexhaustible source of inspiration for millions of countrymen even today.
